Maia for Content repurposing

Turn approved material into drafts for specific channels.

All use cases ↗

Choose the source and boundaries

Content repurposing works best when the team agrees on the source first. Give Maia the final article, approved transcript, or published report. Identify passages that must remain unchanged, claims that require a citation, and material that cannot be reused outside its original setting.

Then define the destination. A customer email needs a clear reason to read and a useful next step. A sales talking point should help a representative explain an idea accurately. A social post must make sense without the surrounding article. Asking for "more content" leaves these decisions unresolved.

Adapt rather than shrink

A shorter version is not always a useful new format. Ask Maia to preserve the source's main claim while changing the structure for the reader and channel. It can pull one example into a post, turn a detailed explanation into a short email sequence, or convert a webinar section into questions a sales team can use.

The output should link each factual statement back to the approved material. If a draft needs a new statistic, testimonial, or product promise, Maia should list it as a gap instead of inventing support.

Keep meaning and rights visible

Repurposing can create subtle errors. A speaker's qualified answer may look categorical once a sentence is removed from the transcript. An image licensed for a report may not be cleared for advertising. An old product description may no longer match the current offer.

Ask Maia to flag these cases for review. The editor checks that the shortened wording still means what the source says. The rights owner confirms that quoted, visual, and third-party material can appear in the new channel.

Review drafts together

Post the draft set in the campaign Slack thread. The editor can reject a weak angle, the product owner can correct a claim, and the channel owner can adjust format requirements. Maia can apply those decisions across the set while keeping each draft distinct.

This workflow stops at reviewed drafts. The team chooses the final copy, recipients, timing, and publishing controls.

Start with one strong asset

Pick a recent piece with clear ownership and useful detail. Create two new formats, check every claim against the source, and note which editorial decisions repeat. Save only durable rules as guidance. A requirement such as "email subject lines must name the reader's task" is reusable. A one-off launch date is not.

Questions from content teams

Will every draft say the same thing?

The underlying facts should agree, but the structure can change with the channel. Give Maia a separate reader, purpose, and length for each output.

Can Maia post the finished content?

This example prepares drafts for review. Publishing stays with the authorized channel owner and the team's existing process.

What if the source is outdated?

Stop and replace or correct it before repurposing. Maia can flag dates and conflicts, but an approved current source must anchor the new drafts.
